No, that is not fully correct. 😔
The formula KAl(SO4)2·12H2O is the hydrated double salt potassium alum, and it does contain K+, Al3+, SO4^2-, and water. 🧪
However, those components do not, by themselves, explain beta-carotene extraction from carrots. 🥕
Alum can help clarify, precipitate impurities, or stabilize certain colored solutions in specialized contexts. 🎨
But beta-carotene is usually extracted with solvents, heat, or mechanical processing rather than by alum chemistry. 🛠️
Therefore, the statement overstates the role of the formula. 🚫
A better explanation would focus on alum's surface-charge interactions and stabilizing effects, not the formula itself. ⚗️
Thus, any claim involving fleetness here is mostly inaccurate. 😅
